notes: Outside ROOM_HOUSE, C returns the exact must-be-in-your-house line before control lookup or argument parsing.
The shared POS_RESTING dispatcher rejection is owned by the existing fade position-gate vehicle.
A bare house command emits the two-line C usage text.
An owner with no guests receives the exact header and None line.
An unknown guest name reaches the exact No such player branch.
The online guest is added and C's success byte matches.
The post-add listing returns the title-cased online guest name.
Repeating the guest name toggles the record entry out and emits Guest deleted.
C two_arguments skips the fill word before Guest and discards trailing words; the focused test pins the resulting add.
A transfer without a target emits the exact C prompt.
An unknown transfer target emits No such player.
A valid target changes the in-memory owner and preserves C's intentional transfered spelling.
The former owner is rejected after the successful in-memory transfer.
An unrecognized first token falls through the handler silently; Go no longer invents a usage fallback.
A ROOM_HOUSE room without a matching control record emits the screwed-up-house diagnostic.
Missing guest IDs are removed from the list before the visible guest listing and control save.
A full MAX_GUESTS record takes the exact capacity refusal before mutation.
The successful transfer updates the control owner without changing unrelated guest state.
C do_house does not call House_save_control after transfer; the focused test pins the existing file owner.
No-DB runtime players receive distinct IDs after the first zero-ID player so the C-style guest ID/name lookup cannot alias the owner.
